selected.name: Gravelmouth
selected.description: Gravelmouth is a broad lake swimmer with short steering flippers and a muscular tapering rear body. Its rounded head and blunt mouth test a heavy aquatic plant grazer without external filtering ornaments.

selected.name: Woodland breaker
selected.description: A deep-chested forest animal braces a fallen trunk with massive claws beneath a blunt beaked head. Its feeding could leave cavities for smaller lives, without making it a deliberate habitat builder.

selected.name: Salt-flat migrant
selected.description: Long jointed legs carry a narrow body and a low-reaching soft-lipped head across open ground. This proposes a migratory grazer shaped by dry crossings and scattered feeding sites.

selected.name: Split-muzzle burrower
selected.description: The plated, shaggy burrower is approved with a clear back and no dorsal sack. Its divided digging muzzle and heavy forelimbs are retained; detailed feeding and breeding biology remain open.

selected.name: Gall glider
selected.description: The furred plant-nursery animal and its opened gliding membranes are approved. Preserve the fine muzzle, mottled coat and gall-dwelling young; the exact physiology remains open.

selected.name: Cradle thief
selected.description: The revised coat is approved: quieter brown sides and a dark dorsal stripe distinguish Cradle thief from the gall glider. Its brood-parasitic role is retained, with the host species still open.

selected.name: Crested bird
selected.description: This long-legged crested bird is approved as an ordinary independent bird. Preserve its curved bill and feather pattern; do not give it the earlier stolen-egg or brood-parasite role.

selected.name: Ford-thread
selected.description: The large translucent aquatic body with the small swimmer's rounded face is approved. Its diet and life cycle remain open.

selected.name: Shore hunter
selected.description: The scale-backed, soft-necked fish-eating shore hunter is approved as a separate animal. It never grows from or transforms into the translucent parasite.

selected.name: Chest-pouch herd animal
selected.description: The accessible underslung chest pouch is approved. This is a small herd with varied responsibilities, not a hive; retain the reaching mouthparts and uninterrupted dorsal covering.
